surfaces.name: asset
surfaces.title: Asset
surfaces.description:
Daemon-side asset events. `Got` and `NotFound` resolve a webapp `Get`
(correlated by request_id). `Ready` broadcasts to all connected
webapps whenever the cache gains an asset, regardless of source
(companion push, iAP2 FileTransfer, request fulfilment, lazy disk
load). `Cleared` broadcasts on every eviction path - LRU pressure,
TTL expiry, companion-issued Clear, daemon shutdown - so SDK
consumers can drop Blob URLs and refetch as needed.

requests.description:
Webapp request: read an asset by id. Bridge replies with `Got` on hit
or `NotFound` (domain) when neither cache nor companion has it.

surfaces.name: audio
surfaces.title: Audio
surfaces.description:
Daemon -> webapp audio events: TTS lifecycle notifications and
volume/mute changes.

surfaces.name: bluetooth
surfaces.title: Bluetooth
surfaces.description:
Daemon -> webapp bluetooth surface: connection status/events,
in-flight pairing feedback, and the reply to `bluetooth.list`.

requests.description:
Marker request: webapp asks the bridge for the paired bluetooth
devices map. Pairs with `BridgeToClientBluetoothMsg::PairedDevices`.

surfaces.name: capabilities
surfaces.title: Capabilities
surfaces.description:
Daemon -> webapp capabilities surface. `Update` is the broadcast event
fired on connect + on every change; `Snapshot` is the typed reply to
`CapabilitiesGet`. Webapps that auto-react to capability change
listen on `Update` and don't need to call `Get`.

requests.description:
One-shot query: webapp asks the daemon for the current capabilities
snapshot. The daemon also broadcasts `Update` on every connect and
on every change, so most webapps don't need this.

surfaces.name: config
surfaces.title: Config
surfaces.description:
Daemon -> webapp config replies and events. `Get` / `List` reply to
the matching requests. `Changed` broadcasts whenever the gateway
writes or deletes a value for the active webapp.

requests.description:
Webapp request: read one config value for the currently active webapp,
as most recently set by the gateway. This surface is read-only; only
the gateway can write config.

Marker request: webapp asks for every config entry the gateway has
set for the currently active webapp.

surfaces.name: doc
surfaces.title: Doc
surfaces.description:
Daemon -> webapp doc replies and events. `Changed` broadcasts whenever
the companion writes or deletes a doc value for the active webapp.

requests.description: Webapp request: read one doc value for the currently active webapp.
Marker request: read every doc entry for the currently active webapp.

Webapp request: write a doc value. Last write wins against companion
writes on the same key; the companion hears the change as a gateway
`webapp.docChanged` event.
Webapp request: delete the doc entry at `key`.

surfaces.name: geo
surfaces.title: Geo
surfaces.description:
Daemon -> webapp location surface: the `Position` stream a watch
produces, plus replies to `geo.watch` and `geo.getOnce`.

surfaces.name: hardware
surfaces.title: Hardware
surfaces.description:
Daemon -> webapp hardware surface: ambient-light and backlight
change events, plus the reply to `hardware.stateGet`.

requests.description:
Webapp asks for the current `HardwareState` snapshot (backlight mode
/ level, ambient light reading).

surfaces.name: library
surfaces.title: Library
surfaces.description:
Daemon -> webapp replies and events for the library surface. `BrowseReply`, `SearchReply`,
`RecommendationsReply`, `ResolveContextReply`, `FavoritesListReply`, and
`FavoritesContainsReply` answer the
matching `ClientToBridgeLibraryMsg` request; `LibraryErrorReply` replaces the reply on
failure. `FavoriteChanged` is a live event broadcast to every connected webapp whenever a
favorite's status changes.

requests.description:
Payload for the `browse` request: page through a folder in the library tree, or the root
menu when `node_id` is `None`. Root-level results are cached by the daemon for up to 5
minutes, so a fresh call immediately after a library change on the gateway side may still
return the previous shelf layout.
Payload for the `search` request: free-text search across the connected gateway's library.

Recommendations seeded by up to 5 items. Spotify hard-caps at 5
combined seeds across tracks/artists/genres.

Payload for the `resolveContext` request: turn a context uri into something renderable.
The uri a webapp holds is usually `PlayerState::context`, so this is what backs a
"playing from <playlist>" line without having to browse for the containing entity.

Payload for the `favoritesList` request: page through the user's saved/liked library items,
mixed across kinds.

Batch "is each of these favorited?" lookup. Reply `liked` is
index-aligned with the request `uris`, capped at 50 per call.

surfaces.name: net
surfaces.title: Net
surfaces.description:
Daemon -> webapp network surface: replies to `fetch` and `ws.open`,
WebSocket frame/close/error events, and the `Stream*` event trio
driven by `net.stream.open`.

requests.description:
Payload for `net.fetch`: a single proxied HTTP request/response
round-trip through the connected companion's network stack.

surfaces.name: notifications
surfaces.title: Notifications
surfaces.description:
Daemon -> webapp notification mirror. `Posted` fires for a new
notification, `Updated` when an existing one's content changes, and
`Removed` when it is dismissed, acted on, or cleared remotely.

surfaces.name: peer
surfaces.title: Peer
surfaces.description:
Daemon -> webapp peer surface: a full snapshot of every known peer
(paired, iAP2, and companion-gateway state), re-sent whenever any
peer changes. There is no per-webapp request; a fresh snapshot
arrives on connect and after every change.

surfaces.name: phone
surfaces.title: Phone
surfaces.description:
Daemon -> webapp telephony surface. `CallStarted`/`CallUpdated`/
`CallEnded`/`CommunicationsChanged` are unsolicited broadcasts driven by
the connected companion's telephony state; `StateReply`/`ErrorReply`
answer webapp-issued requests and commands.

surfaces.name: player
surfaces.title: Player
surfaces.description:
Daemon -> webapp player surface. `Snapshot` lands on connect with the
current player state; `Delta` is the `NowPlayingUpdate` stream the
SDK auto-merges; `QueueChanged` fires when the queue mutates without
a track change. `StateReply`/`QueueReply` are the typed responses
to the matching webapp queries.

requests.description:
Webapp asks for the current `PlayerState` snapshot. Most webapps
don't need this - the SDK auto-merges deltas into a cached state.

Webapp asks for the current queue snapshot. Rarely needed - the SDK
tracks the queue from `QueueChanged` events.
Webapp asks for the provider's remote endpoints

commands.description: Start playback of a uri, optionally within a context.
Add a uri to the queue.
Skip to the previous track, or restart the current one.
Jump to a specific queue index.
Move playback to one of the provider's remote endpoints.

surfaces.name: system
surfaces.title: System
surfaces.description:
Daemon -> webapp system events and replies. `Version` replies to
`VersionRequest` with the daemon's `BridgeThingMeta`. `DiagnosticsReply`,
`LogsTailReply`, `LogsSubscribeReply`, and `DeviceNickname` are replies
to their matching requests. `LogEntry` streams matching lines to a live
`LogsSubscribe` subscription. `OtaProgress` / `OtaError` report OTA
orchestrator state. `DeviceNicknameChanged` broadcasts whenever the
nickname mutates, including from another surface.

requests.description:
Marker request: webapp asks the bridge for its `BridgeThingMeta`.
Pairs with `BridgeToClientSystemMsg::Version`.

Marker request: webapp asks for a one-shot `Diagnostics` snapshot
(disk/memory usage, uptime, SoC temp, load average, versions).
Pairs with `BridgeToClientSystemMsg::DiagnosticsReply`.

surfaces.name: time
surfaces.title: Time
surfaces.description:
Daemon -> webapp wall-clock surface: an initial snapshot at
announce, `Changed` events on tz/locale/clock updates, and the
reply to `time.get`.

requests.description:
Webapp asks for the current `TimeSnapshot` (wall clock + locale +
timezone). Most webapps don't need this - the daemon also pushes
`Changed` events on the same shape whenever the source updates.
Webapp asks for the current `VoiceState` (muted / capturing).

surfaces.name: webapp
surfaces.title: Webapp
surfaces.description:
Daemon -> webapp replies and events for the webapp-management surface. `ListReply`,
`CurrentReply`, `ActiveReply`, and `IconReply` answer the matching `ClientToBridgeWebappMsg`
request; `WebappError` replaces the reply on failure. `WebappInstalled` is a live event
broadcast to every connected webapp whenever an installed-webapp transfer completes.

events.description: event: a webapp install completed successfully

requests.description: Webapp asks which webapp (if any) is currently active in the kiosk.

Payload for the `activate` request: switch the kiosk to the given webapp. The kiosk runs
exactly one webapp at a time, so the daemon navigates it away from whatever was previously
active.

Fetch the icon bytes for an installed webapp. Returns the raw bytes
declared by the manifest's `icon` field.

Webapp asks for lyrics of whatever is playing right now. Deliberately payload-free: the
daemon builds the track identity from its own player state, so a webapp cannot disagree with
it about what is playing.
Webapp request: read a value out of KV storage by key.
Webapp request: write a value to KV storage under `key`.
Webapp request: delete the KV storage entry at `key`.

AcceptCallAction.description:
Direction the accessory wants iOS to take when answering an incoming
call while another call is active.

variants.name: Accept
variants.description:
Answer the new call (placing any existing active call on hold if
telephony allows it).

variants.name: EndAndAccept
variants.description: End the existing active call and answer the new one.

fields.name: artworkId
fields.description: Opaque artwork asset id (`asset.get`), when known.

AmbientLightUpdate.description:
0..=100 ambient-brightness indicator derived from the on-board ALS +
backlight curve. Low = dark room, high = bright room.

ArtProfile.description:
Art render sizes a webapp declares so the companion warms exactly the
pixels it renders: hero (now-playing / detail views) and thumb (queue /
grid). Omitted in a manifest falls back to the canonical `{248, 96}`

fields.name: artworkId
fields.description: Opaque artwork asset id (`asset.get`), when known.

AssetCleared.description:
An asset was evicted from the cache; webapps should drop any cached
Blob URL for it and refetch on next use.

AssetGet.description:
Webapp request: read an asset by id. Bridge replies with `Got` on hit
or `NotFound` (domain) when neither cache nor companion has it.

fields.name: id
fields.description:
Opaque asset id, e.g. `iap2/art/<track-key>/<content-hash>` for iAP2 art
or a companion-defined shape like `spotify/img/<id>`.

fields.name: requestId
fields.description: Correlates the `Got` or `NotFound` reply back to this request.

AssetGot.description: Successful reply to `AssetGet`: the requested bytes.

fields.name: requestId
fields.description: Echoes the `AssetGet.request_id` this reply resolves.

fields.name: id
fields.description: Echoes the requested asset id.

fields.name: bytes
fields.description:
Raw asset bytes, already reassembled if the companion sent them as a
chunked BT transfer.

fields.name: mime
fields.description: Best-effort content type; `None` when the source didn't provide one.

AssetNotFound.description:
Domain-error reply to `AssetGet`: neither the cache nor a connected
companion has an asset for this id.

fields.name: requestId
fields.description: Echoes the `AssetGet.request_id` this reply resolves.

fields.name: id
fields.description: Echoes the requested asset id.

AssetPreload.description:
Webapp hint to warm the asset cache for a set of ids so subsequent
`Get` calls hit cache. Fire-and-forget; webapps observe completion
via `Asset.Ready` events.

fields.name: ids
fields.description:
Ids to prefetch, capped at 64 per call. Ids already cached and ids
under the `iap2/art/` prefix are skipped, since iAP2 art only ever
arrives via a push from the phone, not a pull request.

AssetReady.description:
An asset became fetchable in the cache; a subsequent `AssetGet` for this
id will resolve without a companion round trip.

BluetoothInterface.description:
Describes the device's own bluetooth adapter. `interface` is the
host-side interface name (e.g. `hci0`).

BluetoothPairingResult.description: Outcome of an in-flight pairing attempt initiated by a peer device.

BluetoothPin.description:
A pairing PIN a peer device is displaying, for a webapp to show as
on-screen confirmation.

BluetoothStatus.description: Whether a companion phone is currently connected over bluetooth.

fields.name: wakewordModelVersion
fields.description: None when no wake word model resolved, or when the one that did carries no version stamp.

variants.name: Auto
variants.description: Daemon drives backlight from the on-board ALS.

variants.name: Manual
variants.description: Webapp drives backlight directly via `setLevel`.

BrightnessState.description:
Backlight state. `level` is the user-set value (only respected in
`Manual`); `effective_level` is what's actually on the panel - equal
to `level` in `Manual`, ALS-derived in `Auto`.

BrowseEntry.description:
One row in a `BrowseResult`: either a folder (drilldown) or a leaf
item the user can play / queue / favorite.

BrowseFolder.description:
A drilldown node. `node_id` is opaque and gateway-defined; webapps
pass it back as the next `browse({ node_id })` to descend. `total` is
the count of children behind this folder when the gateway can cheaply
expose it. `preview_children` is an inline first-N slice of those
children so home-shelf shapes don't need a separate drill round-trip;
gateways populate it when cheap (Spotify Web API home shelves include
previews; Apple Music curated rails do too) and leave it `None`
otherwise.

BrowseResult.description:
Page of browse results. `total` is the count of items in the
underlying collection when the gateway can cheaply expose it (None
means indeterminate). `has_more` is the authoritative end-of-data
signal - webapps paginate by raising `offset` until `has_more` is
false rather than relying on `total`.

CallEndReason.description:
Why a call ended, surfaced on `onPhoneCallEnded`. `Failed` carries a
platform-defined reason (network, busy, etc.).

CapabilitiesSnapshot.description:
Wrapper carrying one `Capabilities` snapshot; reply to `CapabilitiesGet`
and payload of the `Update` broadcast event.

CommunicationsState.description:
What call-control verbs are currently legal. Webapps must gate UI on
these flags; sending an unavailable verb is a protocol violation, not
a no-op. All `None` = no signal received yet, treat as conservatively
unavailable.

ConfigChanged.description:
Broadcast when the gateway writes a new value for the active webapp.
`value: None` means the entry was deleted; consumers should fall back
to whatever default they declared.

ConfigEntry.description:
One key/value pair as exposed by config read APIs. `value` is always a
string; consumers parse per the field's declared kind (number -> parseFloat,
boolean -> "true"/"false", string/enum/secret -> as-is).

ConfigField.description:
One declared user-tunable setting. Adjacent-tagged on the wire:
`{"type":"string","data":{"key":"zip",...}}`.

ConfigGet.description:
Webapp request: read one config value for the currently active webapp,
as most recently set by the gateway. This surface is read-only; only
the gateway can write config.

fields.name: value
fields.description: `None` when the gateway has never set this key, as opposed to an empty string.

ConnectBluetooth.description:
Payload for `bluetooth.connect`: connect to an already-paired
device by MAC.

ConnectedDevice.description: The bluetooth device currently connected to the daemon.

CurrentlyActiveApplication.description: The foreground app driving playback, surfaced on iOS over iAP2.

fields.name: id
fields.description: Bundle identifier, e.g. `com.spotify.client`.

DismissReason.description:
Why a notification went away. `Acted` covers both positive and
negative invokes; gateways that distinguish dismiss-vs-acted may
surface both as `Acted`.

DisplaySetLevel.description:
Set the manual backlight level. Ignored unless `mode == Manual`;
callers should pair with `setMode({ Manual })` when forcing a level.

fields.name: level
fields.description: Backlight level in `[0.0, 1.0]`.

DisplaySetMode.description:
Payload for `hardware.displaySetMode`: switch backlight control
between daemon-driven (`Auto`, following the ALS) and webapp-driven
(`Manual`, via `displaySetLevel`).

DocAck.description: Ack for `DocSet` / `DocDelete`; echoes what's now stored.

DocChanged.description:
Broadcast when the COMPANION writes the active webapp's doc namespace.
Webapp-origin writes are not echoed back (the writer already holds the
ack).

fields.name: value
fields.description: `None` means the entry was deleted.

DocDelete.description: Webapp request: delete the doc entry at `key`.

DocEntry.description:
One key/value pair from a webapp's doc namespace: shared structured
state writable from both the companion (gateway) and the webapp
itself, last write wins. Values are strings; apps encode JSON as
needed.

DocGet.description: Webapp request: read one doc value for the currently active webapp.

fields.name: value
fields.description: `None` when the key has never been written.

DocSet.description:
Webapp request: write a doc value. Last write wins against companion
writes on the same key; the companion hears the change as a gateway
`webapp.docChanged` event.

DtmfTone.description: DTMF tones the accessory can play during an active call.

EndCallAction.description: Direction the accessory wants iOS to take when ending a call.

variants.name: End
variants.description: End / decline the call referenced by `CallUUID`.

variants.name: EndAll
variants.description: End every active call.

FavoritesPage.description:
Page of the user's favorited / liked / saved library items. Mixed-kind
because most platforms expose one "Saved" surface across kinds.

ForgetBluetooth.description:
Payload for `bluetooth.forget`: unpair a device and drop it from
the daemon's known-device set.

GeoAccuracy.description:
Subscriber's accuracy preference. `Coarse` opts into the lower-power
city-block-grade fix on platforms that distinguish (iOS reduced
accuracy, Android `PRIORITY_BALANCED_POWER_ACCURACY`). The daemon
aggregates across subscribers and forwards the most-demanding to the
companion.

variants.name: PermissionDenied
variants.description:
The user denied location to the companion app, or the OS gate
refuses (e.g. iOS Always/WhenInUse not granted).

variants.name: NotDeclared
variants.description:
The running webapp's manifest does not list the `geo` permission, so
the daemon refused before involving the phone.

variants.name: Unavailable
variants.description:
Companion is connected but cannot produce a fix (no GPS, airplane
mode, indoors with no fallback).

variants.name: UnknownToken
variants.description: The supplied subscription token is unknown to the daemon.

GeoWatchReply.description:
Watch handle. Webapps pass the token back as
`ClientToBridgeGeoMsg::Unwatch { token }` to release the watch.

HardwareState.description:
Snapshot of the device's hardware-controlled surfaces. Sent on
`hardware.state.get` and re-broadcast on any change. `ambient_level`
is the 0-255 ambient light reading.

HttpHeader.description:
One header on an HTTP request or response. Key order is preserved
across serialize/deserialize.

InitiateCallType.description: What kind of outbound call the accessory wants placed.

ItemKind.description:
Coarse type tag a webapp uses to filter or branch. Mirrors the variant
names of `LibraryItem`; kept separate so search/recommendations can
constrain by kind without having to construct a sample item.

ItemRef.description:
Stable URI + kind a webapp passes back to act on a library item
(e.g. `player.play({ uri })`, `library.favorites.toggle({ item })`).
`persistent_id` is the platform-stable id when the gateway has one;
webapps treat it as opaque.

KVDelete.description: Webapp request: delete the KV storage entry at `key`.

KVGet.description: Webapp request: read a value out of KV storage by key.

KVPut.description: Webapp request: write a value to KV storage under `key`.

LibraryBrowse.description:
Payload for the `browse` request: page through a folder in the library tree, or the root
menu when `node_id` is `None`. Root-level results are cached by the daemon for up to 5
minutes, so a fresh call immediately after a library change on the gateway side may still
return the previous shelf layout.

fields.name: nodeId
fields.description: Folder to descend into, from a prior result's `BrowseFolder::node_id`. `None` browses the root.

fields.name: limit
fields.description: Requested page size; the daemon clamps this to 100 regardless of the value sent.

fields.name: sections
fields.description: Root only: cap on the number of folders returned. `None` returns every folder.

fields.name: preview
fields.description:
Root only: preview children per folder. `None` is the gateway default; `0` skips preview
hydration entirely and returns a cheap index of node ids, titles, and totals.

variants.name: NotFound
variants.description: The named uri or node id does not exist in the gateway's library.

variants.name: NotSupported
variants.description:
The operation isn't supported by the underlying source (e.g. a
platform that exposes browse but not recommendations).

variants.name: Unauthorized
variants.description: User account / OAuth scope does not permit the operation.

variants.name: NoGateway
variants.description: No companion is connected to back the surface.

LibraryFavoritesContains.description:
Batch "is each of these favorited?" lookup. Reply `liked` is
index-aligned with the request `uris`, capped at 50 per call.

fields.name: uris
fields.description: Uris to check; the daemon truncates this to the first 50 regardless of the count sent.

fields.name: liked
fields.description: Index-aligned with the request's `uris`.

LibraryFavoritesList.description:
Payload for the `favoritesList` request: page through the user's saved/liked library items,
mixed across kinds.

fields.name: limit
fields.description: Requested page size; the daemon clamps this to 100 regardless of the value sent.

LibraryItem.description:
One playable / browsable item from the library. Lean per-variant
payload - gateways translate platform-specific extras down to these
fields, rare per-platform fields just don't surface. Forward-compat:
adding new variants or fields is an additive change webapps can
branch on.

LibraryRecommendations.description:
Recommendations seeded by up to 5 items. Spotify hard-caps at 5
combined seeds across tracks/artists/genres.

fields.name: seeds
fields.description: Seed items; the daemon truncates this to the first 5 regardless of the count sent.

fields.name: kind
fields.description: Restrict results to this item kind. `None` lets the gateway choose based on the seeds.

fields.name: limit
fields.description: Requested page size; the daemon clamps this to 100 regardless of the value sent.

LibraryResolveContext.description:
Payload for the `resolveContext` request: turn a context uri into something renderable.
The uri a webapp holds is usually `PlayerState::context`, so this is what backs a
"playing from <playlist>" line without having to browse for the containing entity.

LibraryResolveContextReply.description:
Reply to `resolveContext`. Every field is best-effort: a gateway that recognises the uri but
cannot cheaply name it answers with `None`s rather than failing the request.

LibrarySearch.description: Payload for the `search` request: free-text search across the connected gateway's library.

fields.name: kinds
fields.description: Restrict results to these item kinds. `None` searches every kind.

fields.name: limit
fields.description: Requested page size; the daemon clamps this to 100 regardless of the value sent.

LyricLine.description:
One timed line. `start_ms` is relative to track start, so a webapp highlights against the
same clock it draws the progress bar from.

Lyrics.description:
Lyrics for one track. `synced` and `plain` are independent: a source may carry either, both,
or neither. `source` names the provider so a webapp can attribute it.

MediaItem.description:
Currently-playing track, populated to the extent the gateway/iAP2
stream has surfaced. All fields are optional because each one arrives
as a separate attribute fetch on iAP2; the daemon accumulates and the
snapshot reflects whatever's known so far.

MediaItemUpdate.description:
Per-track attributes that vary per song. `persistent_id` is a stable
per-platform identifier (iAP2 sends u64; we hex-encode it on the
wire). `artwork_id` is an opaque asset id - webapps pass this value
to `ClientToBridgeAssetMsg::Get` to retrieve the bytes. The id namespace
is producer-defined: iAP2 emits `iap2/art/<track_key>/<content_hash>`, the
companion picks whatever shape it wants (e.g. `spotify/track/<id>/image`).
Webapps treat the value as opaque.

MediaType.description:
The kind of media currently playing. Multi-typed: an item can be
e.g. both `Podcast` and `AudioBook` (rare). Drives webapp UI choices
like skip-15s-vs-skip-track and chapter UI.

NetFetch.description:
Payload for `net.fetch`: a single proxied HTTP request/response
round-trip through the connected companion's network stack.

Notification.description:
One notification surfaced from the connected companion's notification
center. `id` is companion-stable for the lifetime of the notification
- webapps pass it to `invokePositive`/`invokeNegative` and listen for
`onNotificationRemoved`. Bodies (`title`/`subtitle`/`message`) are all
optional because ANCS treats them as separate attribute fetches.

NotificationAction.description:
One ANCS-style action slot. `label` is the gateway-localized prompt
the webapp renders on the action button.

NotificationApp.description:
Originating app metadata. `bundle_id` is platform-stable
(`com.apple.MobileSMS`, `com.spotify.client`, etc.); `display_name`
and `icon_asset_id` are best-effort and may be missing on Android
gateways that don't surface them cheaply.

NotificationFlags.description:
ANCS-shaped flags. `silent` mirrors the iOS "do not surface
audibly" hint and `important` is the high-importance flag. Only
notifications posted while the daemon is connected are surfaced, so
there is no pre-existing/backfill marker.

NotificationsError.description:
Why a notification action slot could not be invoked. Both invoke verbs are
fire-and-forget commands, so a refusal has no reply to ride on.

variants.name: NotFound
variants.description: The id is no longer in the companion's active notification set.

variants.name: ActionRejected
variants.description: The slot is absent on this notification, or the platform refused it.

variants.name: NoTarget
variants.description: No companion is connected, so there is nowhere to send the action.

NowPlayingUpdate.description:
Delta event the companion or iAP2 stream emits whenever a player
attribute changes. Every field is optional: producers send partial
updates populating only what changed, and fields left unset keep
their prior value.

fields.name: updateId
fields.description: which update failed. a resume re-drives the same artifact, so this is NOT unique per attempt.

fields.name: replayed
fields.description: set only when the bridge is re-delivering a failure whose peer had already gone away

OtaErrorCode.description: Terminal error from the OTA orchestrator

variants.name: UnknownUpdate
variants.description: Companion sent fragments for an `update_id` that was never begun

variants.name: OffsetMismatch
variants.description: A fragment's offset did not match the daemon's `received`.

variants.name: HashMismatch
variants.description: Streamed total's sha256 did not match `OtaBegin.transfer.sha256`.

variants.name: SizeMismatch
variants.description: Streamed total's byte length did not match `OtaBegin.transfer.total_size`.

variants.name: Cancelled
variants.description: `CancelUpdate` arrived during a cancelable phase.

variants.name: WriteFailed
variants.description: libswupdate rejected the .swu (parse / handler / I/O failure).

variants.name: ConfirmFailed
variants.description: Slot-flip / try-counter reset failed after a successful write.

variants.name: Internal
variants.description: Anything else (transfer-cache I/O, internal channel close, etc.).

OtaFinished.description: Terminal success from the OTA orchestrator, emitted for every `OtaKind`.

OtaKind.description: What the streamed bytes are going to be applied as

OtaPhase.description:
Stage of the OTA orchestrator. The phase set is shared between
kinds, with non-image kinds emitting a subset

PhoneCall.description:
One telephony call. `call_id` is companion-stable for the call's
lifetime; webapps pass it back to `answer`/`decline`/`end`/`hold`.
`remote_id` is the raw E.164 (or platform raw); `display_name` is the
gateway's resolved contact name when available.

PhoneCallService.description:
Call bearer / service kind. iAP2's `CallStateUpdateService` enum
values, projected to our wire surface. Companion gateways that don't
distinguish bearers project all calls to `Telephony`.

PhoneCommunicationsReply.description:
Broadcast whenever `CommunicationsState` changes: signal, registration,
or which call-control verbs are currently legal.

variants.name: CallNotFound
variants.description: The supplied `call_id` is not in the daemon's active set.

variants.name: ActionRejected
variants.description:
The companion or platform refused the action (e.g. answer while no
ringing call exists, end on a remote-controlled conference leg).

variants.name: NoTarget
variants.description:
No iAP2 link or companion attached, so there's nowhere to send the
outbound action.

variants.name: Unavailable
variants.description: `*Available` flag for this verb was false at action time.

PhoneState.description:
Snapshot of every active call known to the gateway. Multi-call is
possible (call-waiting, conference) - webapps rendering only one
active call typically pick the first non-Held entry.

PlayContext.description:
Optional context for `play({ uri })`. `context_uri` is the album /
playlist / show URI the track is being played from; gateways with
playlist support honor it for skip-next semantics. A row inside the
context is addressed by playing that row's own uri within it, so there
is no index here.

Playback.description:
Per-session playback snapshot: where in the song we are, what mode is
engaged. `position_ms` is the live playhead at snapshot time; webapps
extrapolate forward locally while `state == Playing`.

`set_elapsed_time_available` gates scrub UI: when false, the foreground
app refuses absolute-position seeks and webapps must disable the scrub
thumb. `None` means unknown (no signal received yet); webapps treat
unknown as "available" for backward compatibility with older gateways.

PlaybackContext.description:
What the current track is playing from: the playlist / album / show /
artist context. Webapps render "playing from <name>"; `uri` lets them
drill into it. `name` is `None` until the companion resolves it.

PlaybackTarget.description:
A remote endpoint the current provider can move playback to. Only
meaningful when `SurfaceAvailability::playback_targets` is set.

`volume_percent` is `None` when the endpoint does not report volume.

fields.name: id
fields.description: Provider-opaque endpoint id; pass back to `transferTo`.

fields.name: isActive
fields.description: Whether this endpoint is the one currently playing.

PlaybackTargetKind.description:
What kind of endpoint a `PlaybackTarget` is. Coarse on purpose: the
provider vocabularies (Spotify Connect, AirPlay, Cast) do not agree in
their long tails, and webapps only pick an icon from this. Anything
unrecognized maps to `Unknown` rather than leaking a provider string.

PlaybackUpdate.description:
Per-playback-session attributes that vary regardless of track:
playing/paused, position, shuffle/repeat, and the iOS bundle
identifier of the app currently driving playback (e.g.
`"com.spotify.client"`). `app_bundle` is null on the Android path
since it isn't a meaningful surface there.

`set_elapsed_time_available` is the gate webapps must honor for
scrub UI: when false, scrubbing is unsupported by the foreground
app and the seek button must be disabled.

variants.name: SchemeUnclaimed
variants.description:
`play({uri})` was called with a scheme no connected gateway claims.
Returned synchronously by the daemon without round-tripping.

variants.name: PlayFailed
variants.description: Gateway acknowledged the verb but couldn't fulfill it.

variants.name: NoGateway
variants.description: No companion is connected.

variants.name: NotInQueue
variants.description: `skipToIndex` referenced a queue index that doesn't exist.

variants.name: UnknownTarget
variants.description: `transferTo` named an endpoint that is not in the current target list.

PlayerOptions.description:
User-tunable knobs that are not "currently playing" state.
`crossfade_ms = None` is "crossfade off"; `Some(0)` is also off but
distinguishes "user explicitly set zero" from "feature unsupported by
gateway".

PlayerQueueReply.description: Response to `queueGet`, also carried by the `QueueChanged` event.

fields.name: current
fields.description: The now-playing track, when one is loaded.

fields.name: items
fields.description: Upcoming tracks in queue order.

fields.name: previous
fields.description: Recently-played history.

PlayerState.description:
Full player snapshot the daemon broadcasts to webapps. Initial value
arrives on `BridgeToClientPlayerMsg::StateChange` at connect time;
subsequent changes flow as `NowPlayingUpdate` deltas the client SDK
merges into the cached snapshot.

PlayerStateReply.description: Response to `stateGet`, also carried by the `Snapshot` event.

fields.name: activeApp
fields.description: The app currently driving playback, when known (iOS surfaces this over iAP2).

PlayerTargetsReply.description: Response to `targetsGet`, also carried by the `TargetsChanged` event.

Playlist.description:
Lean cross-platform shape for a playlist. `uri` is what `player.play`
would route on; `track_count` is best-effort (some sources don't expose
it cheaply); `owner_name` is whatever the source surfaces (Spotify
owner, Apple Music curator, etc.).

PodcastEpisode.description:
One episode of a podcast. `show_name` mirrors what the gateway exposes
at episode-level so a webapp can render show + episode without a
separate fetch. `published_at_ms` is best-effort; not every gateway
surfaces it.

Position.description:
One position fix from the gateway. `accuracy_m` is the 1-sigma
horizontal radius. `speed_mps` and `heading_deg` are populated when
the underlying source provides them (CLLocation on iOS does for moving
fixes; Android's FusedLocationProvider similar). `ts_ms` is the
gateway-provided fix timestamp, not the wire-arrival time.

QueueItem.description:
One row in the player queue. Lean cross-platform shape - gateways
that have richer per-track data still surface what fields they have.
`uri` is required because every queued item must be addressable for
`skipToIndex`. `persistent_id` is the platform-stable id when
available; webapps treat it as opaque.

QueuePosition.description:
Where in the queue a `queue({ uri })` should land. `Append` (default)
goes at the end; `Next` is play-next; `Index(n)` is an explicit 0-based slot
in the upcoming list.

RecommendationsResult.description:
Page of recommendation results. Gateway decides how seed + kind
interact (Spotify uses radio-style seeding, Apple Music uses curated
rails) - the daemon doesn't prescribe.

variants.name: Follow
variants.description: Follow up to a gateway-defined cap (typically 5).

variants.name: Manual
variants.description: Surface the redirect status to the caller; do not follow.

variants.name: Error
variants.description: Treat any 3xx as an error.

RegistrationStatus.description:
Cellular registration state - populated from iAP2 `CommunicationsUpdate`
or the companion's equivalent.

RepeatMode.description:
`repeat` is a typed enum (Off/All/One) shared across the player
surface and the iAP2 NowPlaying CSM / MediaSession backends, which
all expose three repeat states.

SearchResult.description:
Page of search results. `kinds` is the constrained kinds the search
honored (echoed back so webapps can detect ignored constraints); items
are ranked best-first.

SetBluetoothAlias.description:
Payload for `bluetooth.setAlias`: rename the device's own adapter
as seen by peers during discovery and pairing.

Show.description:
One podcast show (parent of `PodcastEpisode`). `episode_count` is
best-effort.

ShuffleMode.description:
Three-state shuffle. iAP2 and Apple Music distinguish track-level
from album-level shuffle; companion gateways without that distinction
project to `Songs` when on. Webapps that just need an on/off signal
read `shuffle_on` (None when the underlying mode is unknown).

SkipPrev.description: Payload for `skipPrev`: go to the previous track, or restart the current one.

fields.name: allowSeeking
fields.description: When true, restart the current track if it is progressed past the restart threshold; otherwise always move to the previous track.

Station.description:
Algorithmic / radio station. `seed` is the URI the station was seeded
from when known (artist, track, etc.).

StorageResponse.description:
Reply to `KVGet`, `KVPut`, and `KVDelete` alike; the request that
produced it distinguishes which operation happened.

fields.name: value
fields.description: `None` on a `Get` miss or after a `Delete`; `Put` always echoes back `Some` of what it just wrote.

StreamBegin.description:
First event of an open stream. Carries the response status, headers,
and (when known) total payload size so the consumer can preallocate
or display progress. Subsequent `StreamChunk` and `StreamEnd` events
for the same `stream_id` follow.

StreamChunk.description:
One body chunk. Chunks arrive in order; `offset` is the byte
position of `bytes[0]` within the full body.

StreamEnd.description:
Terminates a stream. After `End` no further chunks for `stream_id`
are valid and the daemon clears its routing entry.

StreamError.description:
Stream failed mid-flight (or before the first byte). Terminal - the
daemon clears its routing entry. The `error` shape is shared with
`fetch` since the failure modes are identical.

TimeInfo.description:
Wall clock + locale snapshot. `wall_clock_unix_s` is the gateway's
(or iAP2 device's) claimed "now" in unix-epoch seconds - webapps
reading time should use the device clock if any but use this as the
trust anchor on first arrival.

Two zone-identification paths coexist: companion gateways send
`tz_iana` (an IANA zone identifier like `America/Denver`) while iAP2
`DeviceTimeUpdate` only exposes numeric `utc_offset_minutes` plus a
separate `dst_offset_minutes`. Webapps prefer `tz_iana` when present
and fall back to the offset pair.

TimeSnapshot.description:
Wraps `TimeInfo` for the wire; used as both the `time.get` reply and
the `Changed` event payload.

Track.description:
A track with resolved album/artist metadata, used by library search
and browse results. For live now-playing state see `MediaItem`.

fields.name: artist
fields.description: Primary credited artist.

fields.name: artists
fields.description: All credited artists, in order.

fields.name: imageId
fields.description: Opaque artwork asset id; pass to `asset.get` for the bytes.

fields.name: saved
fields.description: Whether the track is saved in the user's library.

VoiceActivity.description: One step of a voice turn, as it happens

VoiceActivityError.description: Why a turn ended without dispatching.

VoiceDispatchTarget.description: Where the daemon actually routed a successful dispatch

variants.name: Playback
variants.description: Transport / playback effect

variants.name: Device
variants.description: A daemon-local device action (discoverable, preset save, cancel).

variants.name: Phone
variants.description: Phone call control over the companion's phone surface.

variants.name: Display
variants.description: Display-shaped intent handed to the active webapp to render.

variants.name: WebappSwitch
variants.description: Switched the active webapp via OPEN_WEBAPP.

VoiceIntent.description: A resolved display intent for the active webapp to render

VoicePhase.description: Where a voice turn is in the pipeline

WebappActivate.description:
Payload for the `activate` request: switch the kiosk to the given webapp. The kiosk runs
exactly one webapp at a time, so the daemon navigates it away from whatever was previously
active.

fields.name: id
fields.description: Id of an installed webapp, from `webapp.list`.

fields.name: id
fields.description: Id of the webapp that was just activated.

fields.name: id
fields.description: `None` when no webapp is currently active in the kiosk.

WebappError.description:
Domain errors emitted by any webapp surface (gateway- or client-side).
Single catalog: both protocols speak the same variant set.

variants.name: WebappNotFound
variants.description: No installed webapp matches this id (uninstall / activate / icon / config target).

variants.name: CannotUninstallBuiltin
variants.description: Built-in webapps cannot be uninstalled.

variants.name: IdReserved
variants.description:
Install rejected: the manifest's id is in the reserved-uuid set
(stock, hub, launcher, etc).

variants.name: ExtractedTooLarge
variants.description: Extracted bundle exceeds the 1 GiB disk-protection cap.

variants.name: ProvenanceTooLong
variants.description: Install carried a provenance string over `WEBAPP_PROVENANCE_MAX_LEN`.

variants.name: ZipMalformed
variants.description: Zip extraction failed: corrupt archive, unsafe entry names, etc.

variants.name: MissingIndexHtml
variants.description: Bundle has no index.html at its root.

variants.name: InvalidManifest
variants.description: manifest.json missing, unparseable, or failed schema validation.

variants.name: ResourceNotAvailable
variants.description:
The requested resource (icon / settings page / overlay) isn't declared
by the webapp's manifest or its file is missing on disk.

variants.name: NotALauncher
variants.description: Launcher slot rejected: the bundle does not declare `role: launcher`.

variants.name: NoOverlay
variants.description: Overlay slot rejected: the bundle declares no overlay entry.

variants.name: UnknownConfigKey
variants.description: Config key is not declared in the webapp's manifest schema.

variants.name: InvalidConfigValue
variants.description: Value failed schema validation (out of range, regex mismatch, not in enum).

variants.name: InvalidDocValue
variants.description: Doc value rejected (oversized).

variants.name: Internal
variants.description:
Catch-all for genuinely-unexpected failures (io errors, daemon-side
bugs). Reason is human-readable; not a stable wire contract.

WebappIcon.description:
Fetch the icon bytes for an installed webapp. Returns the raw bytes
declared by the manifest's `icon` field.

fields.name: id
fields.description: Id of an installed webapp, from `webapp.list`.

WebappIconReply.description: Reply to the `icon` request: the raw icon bytes declared by the webapp's manifest.

fields.name: mime
fields.description: MIME type declared by the manifest's icon; `None` if the manifest didn't declare one.

fields.name: webapps
fields.description: Excludes `Launcher`-role bundles used as alternate home screens.

WebappRole.description:
A webapp's launcher visibility. `Standard` shows up in user-facing
listings (the hub grid, etc); `Launcher` is itself a launcher and is
hidden from those listings. The daemon filters `Launcher` bundles
out of `client.webapp.list`; the gateway list keeps everything.
Declaring `Launcher` is also what makes a bundle eligible for the
device's launcher slot.

WebappUninstalled.description: Broadcast when an installed webapp is removed; carries the removed webapp's name.
